entries.text: v12.6.3 (2026-11-26) Notable changes Testing Test.createTestingModule() accepts the instrument option, like NestFactory.create(). Its instanceDecorator decorates the module's providers, overridden ones included, and the applications and microservices created from the module use it unless their own options set one. Tests can now run an app instrumented as it is in production. With NestJS Observe, for example, gateway tests no longer log that the instrument option is missing – #18743 Instances that an application context creates through resolve() (request-scoped and transient providers) are passed to the instrument instance decorator, in a testing module and in NestFactory.createApplicationContext() – #18743 Behaviour changes Route conflict detection compares paths the way the router matches them. On Express, which matches paths in any case, GET /users and GET /Users are reported as the same route, so duplicate: 'error' aborts bootstrap. The same holds on Fastify with caseSensitive: false. Nothing changes where the router is case-sensitive: Fastify by default, the Node adapter, and Express with case sensitive routing enabled – #18721 A path excluded without a version, in MiddlewareConsumer.exclude() or in the exclude option of enableCsrfProtection(), also covers the routes of the default version(s), as forRoutes() does – #18601 @Body('key') with a falsy primitive body ("", 0, false) yields undefined, like any other primitive body. It used to receive the whole body – #18720 Pars

entries.summary: v12.6.2 (2026-11-25; Fixes of 12.6.1; applyDecorators() type-checks again as a class, method and property decorator. In 12.6.1 its return type became a union that TypeScript rejects where a composed decorator is…
entries.text: v12.6.2 (2026-11-25) Notable changes Fixes of 12.6.1 applyDecorators() type-checks again as a class, method and property decorator. In 12.6.1 its return type became a union that TypeScript rejects where a composed decorator is applied (TS1270), also with skipLibCheck. It now also types as a parameter decorator, which it supports since 12.6.1 – #18710 Behaviour changes @nestjs/platform-node: res.send() pipes a Readable stream, as Fastify's reply.send() does, with application/octet-stream unless a Content-Type is set. It used to send the stream's fields as JSON (e.g. the path of a file stream) and leave the stream open. A stream that fails before anything is sent gets a 500, one that fails midway aborts the response, and the stream is destroyed when the client goes away – #18702 A StreamableFile answered with a 204, 205 or 304 sends no body and is not read, on Express and Node. On Fastify, a 205 response sends no body – #18711, #18713 ParseDatePipe rejects a day past the end of its month in a month-name date without a year (Feb 30, Sep 31). As in new Date(), such a date is in 2001, so Feb 29 is rejected as well – #18699 The missing decorator metadata warning also covers a decorated subclass compiled without metadata (e.g. with tsx or esbuild) that extends a class compiled with it, when a parameter of its own constructor would be injected as undefined – #18698 @nestjs/common exports GetOrResolveOptions, SelectOptions, HttpArgumentsHost, RpcArgumentsHost, WsArgumentsHost, CorsOpt

entries.text: v12.6.1 (2026-11-25) Notable changes New features RabbitMQ server: nackOnInternalError (false by default). With noAck: false, the message of a handler that fails with an internal error (an exception other than an RpcException) is negatively acknowledged without requeue, so a dead letter exchange of the queue receives it. It used to stay unacknowledged until the channel closed – #18686 New defaults and behaviour changes ParseDatePipe rejects more dates that new Date() would roll into the next month: unpadded and dotted numeric dates (2/30/2024), month names (Feb 30, 2024), two-digit years (4/31/24), and dates after a weekday or with other separators (Fri 02/30/2024, 2024 02 30) – #18652, #18673, #18675, #18693 ParseArrayPipe with stopAtFirstError: false collects the exceptions of a custom exceptionFactory that are not an HttpException (e.g. RpcException) for every item again, where since 12.5.0 it threw the first one – #18689 ParseEnumPipe returns an exact match before a numeric one, so '0' gives '0' rather than 0 for an enum that has both – #18649 applyDecorators() uses what a composed decorator returns, as TypeScript does: a returned descriptor replaces the method and a returned class replaces the class. A composed parameter decorator (e.g. applyDecorators(Inject(TOKEN)) on a constructor parameter) gets the parameter's index – #18688 ConsoleLogger redact also masks the entries of Headers, URLSearchParams and FormData, the username, password and search params of a URL, and th

entries.text: What's changed @nestjs/platform-fastify fix(deps): update dependency @fastify/middie to v9.3.8 — #18687, by @anthgrim; a request target that is neither origin-form nor an http(s) absolute-form URL, and that the router didn't match, now gets a 400 (FST_ERR_MIDDIE_MALFORMED_URL) instead of reaching the not-found handler fix(deps): update dependency @fastify/middie to v9.3.9 — backport of #18644; middie now also adds a middleware to the Fastify plugins registered before it, as the adapter already did for Nest middleware, which still runs once per request Node.js version: @fastify/middie 9.3.7 and later load the ES module path-to-regexp 9 with require(), so @nestjs/platform-fastify 11.2.12 needs Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+. On earlier 20.x and 22.x releases, importing it fails with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM. Full Changelog: v11.2.11...v11.2.12

entries.text: v12.6.0 (2026-11-20) Notable changes New features NestFactory.create() infers the application type from the adapter: NestFactory.create(AppModule, new FastifyAdapter()) returns a NestFastifyApplication with no type argument, and the same goes for ExpressAdapter and NodeAdapter. An explicit type argument still works. A custom adapter declares its application type as the fourth type argument of AbstractHttpAdapter – #18623 WsAdapter takes gracefulShutdown (false by default) and gracePeriod (10,000 ms by default). With gracefulShutdown, closing the application stops accepting connections (an upgrade on a server shared with the HTTP adapter gets a 503), ignores new messages, waits up to gracePeriod for message handlers and pending replies, and closes each socket with code 1001 – #18589 gRPC server: gracePeriod (10,000 ms by default) for gracefulShutdown – #18566 New defaults and behaviour changes gRPC server with gracefulShutdown: closing used to wait for the calls in progress with no limit; calls still running after gracePeriod are now cancelled. Raise gracePeriod for long-running streams – #18566 A custom parameter decorator that gives the handler the response object now passes it as it is, and no pipe runs on it, as with @Res(), whatever the adapter. On Fastify such a handler used to never run – #18600 A method that overrides a @Res({ passthrough: true }) handler with a plain @Res() no longer inherits passthrough – #18617 DiscoveryService finds a class that extends a class dec
